text:
On 14 March 2024, the Institute for Northern Codicology released its linguistic analysis of the Voskresen manuscript, and its conclusion is plain: the codex was written in Middle Low German.

I spoke with Dr. Halvard Teskemar, the Institute's lead palaeographer, who directed the study. He told me the team examined all 212 vellum leaves during a 2023 survey of the manuscript. Of those, 187 were confirmed as Middle Low German in both script and vocabulary.

"The evidence is consistent across the bulk of the codex," Dr. Teskemar said. "There is no real doubt about the language."

The findings appear in the Institute's peer-reviewed report, "Language and Provenance of the Voskresen Codex" (Report No. 7), which I have read in part. The report treats the Middle Low German identification as established.

The announcement settles a question that has followed the manuscript for years.
